drug_class: Androgen receptor inhibitor (hormone therapy for prostate cancer)
purpose: Enzalutamide is used to treat prostate cancer. It is used in men whose prostate cancer has spread to other parts of the body or no longer responds well to other treatments. It can be used whether or not the cancer has stopped responding to standard hormone therapy.
how_it_works: Prostate cancer cells need the male hormone testosterone to grow. Enzalutamide works by blocking the receptor on cancer cells that testosterone normally attaches to, so the cancer cells cannot get the signal they need to grow and multiply. Think of it like putting a lock cover over a keyhole so the key cannot get in.
common_side_effects: Tiredness or weakness, hot flashes, high blood pressure, headache, dizziness, swelling in the hands or feet, decreased appetite, diarrhea, back or joint pain, and weight loss are among the most common side effects.
warnings: Enzalutamide can rarely cause seizures, so tell your doctor if you have ever had a seizure or a brain condition. It may cause serious dizziness or falls, especially in older patients. It can cause a rare but serious brain condition called PRES — seek medical help if you have sudden severe headache, vision changes, or confusion. Women who are pregnant or could become pregnant should never handle this medication, as it can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor about all your other medications, as enzalutamide can interact with many common drugs.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 160 mg (four 40 mg capsules or tablets) taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. Swallow the capsules or tablets whole — do not crush or chew them.
